subject: literature
topic: Metre and versification: iambic, trochaic, couplet, quatrain, blank verse

kept.q: Read this line: 'Alone she walked beside the river bend.' What is the name given to a metrical foot made up of one unstressed syllable followed by one stressed syllable, as repeated in this line?
kept.explanation: Each foot here moves from unstressed to stressed, for example 'a-LONE' and 'she WALKED'. This rising pattern is called an iamb.
kept.pidgin: Di way di word dem dey sound, e dey start from soft go strong like 'a-LONE'. Dis kain pattern wey dey rise na wetin dem dey call iamb.

kept.q: A Nigerian poet writes a six-line poem describing market women at Oyingbo, using couplets throughout, with each pair of lines closing on a complete thought before the next pair begins. What term best describes this use of couplets?
kept.explanation: When each couplet expresses a complete, self-contained statement that ends with punctuation, it is called a closed couplet. This differs from couplets whose sense runs on into the next line.
kept.pidgin: If two lines finish one full tori and get punctuation, we dey call am closed couplet. E no be like di ones wey di sense dey flow enter next line.

kept.q: Which of the following best explains why Shakespeare's plays are said to be written mainly in blank verse rather than in rhymed couplets?
options: The lines rhyme in alternating pattern but have no fixed metre
The lines follow unrhymed iambic pentameter, giving a natural speech-like rhythm
The lines have no metre or rhyme at all
The lines are grouped into rhymed quatrains of four stresses each
kept.explanation: Blank verse is unrhymed but keeps a regular metre, usually iambic pentameter. This gives dramatic speech a natural yet elevated rhythm without the constraint of rhyme.
kept.pidgin: Blank verse no get rhyme but e get steady rhythm wey sound like how pesin dey talk. E dey make di drama sound natural but still get class.

kept.q: Scan this line: 'My heart leaps up when I behold a star.' How many metrical feet does this line contain, and what is the dominant foot type?
kept.explanation: Counting the stresses: my HEART, leaps UP, when I, be HOLD, a STAR gives five iambic feet. This makes the line iambic pentameter.
kept.pidgin: If you count di stress for di line, you go see say e get five feet. Because e dey follow di iambic pattern, we dey call am iambic pentameter.

kept.q: A student describes a stanza form as having four lines, with the first and third lines rhyming, and the second and fourth lines rhyming, following an ABAB pattern. What is this stanza form called?
kept.explanation: A four-line stanza is known as a quatrain, regardless of the particular rhyme scheme used. ABAB is one of several common rhyme patterns found in quatrains.
kept.pidgin: Any stanza wey get four lines na quatrain, no matter how di rhyme scheme be. ABAB na just one of di many ways wey dem fit arrange di rhyme.

kept.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes trochaic metre from iambic metre?
options: Trochaic metre stresses the first syllable of each foot, while iambic metre stresses the second
Trochaic metre has no stressed syllables, while iambic metre alternates stress randomly
Trochaic metre is only used in prose, while iambic metre is only used in drama
Trochaic metre always has five feet, while iambic metre always has four feet
kept.explanation: A trochee begins with a stressed syllable followed by an unstressed one, the reverse of an iamb. This difference in stress placement is what separates the two metres.
kept.pidgin: Trochee dey start with strong sound, but iamb dey start with soft sound. Na dis difference for where di stress dey stay make dem different.

kept.q: A critic notes that a certain long narrative poem is composed entirely in unrhymed lines of ten syllables each, with a consistent alternation of unstressed and stressed syllables throughout. Which term most precisely names this verse form?
kept.explanation: Unrhymed lines written consistently in iambic pentameter, meaning ten syllables with regular stress alternation, define blank verse. This distinguishes it from free verse, which lacks a fixed metrical pattern, and from the heroic couplet, which rhymes.
kept.pidgin: If line no get rhyme but e get ten syllables wey dey follow iambic pentameter, na blank verse be dat. E different from free verse because free verse no get fixed rhythm.

q.q: Consider this line: 'DOUble, DOUble, TOIL and TROUble burn.' If the first four syllables each carry a strong stress unlike the surrounding iambic feet, what poetic effect is most likely created by this irregularity?
options: It smooths the rhythm to match ordinary speech
It emphasises urgency and intensity through the heavy, forceful stresses
It signals that the poem has shifted into free verse
It converts the entire line into dactylic metre
q.explanation: Clustering stressed syllables together, as in spondaic substitution, slows the line and creates heaviness. This heightens the sense of urgency or intensity, breaking the normal iambic flow for dramatic effect.

rejected.why: ambiguous:The first four syllables are not all stressed; the line is not otherwise iambic.|
